memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them so they may serve me as priests. Say to the Israelites, 'This is to be my sacred anointing oil for the generations to come. Do not pour it on anyone else's body and do not make any perfume with this formula. It is sacred, and you are to consider it sacred. Whoever makes perfume like it and puts it on anyone other than a priest must be cut off from their people.'" - Exodus 30:30-33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God is emphatic: this oil is not for ordinary use. No one may reproduce the formula for personal perfume, and it may not be poured on just anyone. What was set apart for God must not be treated as common. The penalty for ignoring this was severe.

Behind the strictness is an important principle. Holy things lose their meaning when they are treated casually. If the sacred oil became everyday perfume, its significance would evaporate. God guards what is holy so that it continues to mean something.

We face a subtler version of this danger. The name of God becomes a casual exclamation. Communion becomes routine. Scripture becomes wallpaper. Nothing about these things has changed, but our handling of them has. The writer of Hebrews warns against treating as unholy what is sacred (Heb 10:29). Guard the sacred things in your life. Keep them from sliding into the ordinary through careless familiarity, and ask God to renew your sense of their weight.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
What sacred things have I begun handling casually?
How can I restore a proper sense of reverence for what God calls holy?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me where I have let holy things become common through careless familiarity. Restore my reverence, and help me treat as sacred what You have set apart. Amen.
